text:
Aria: Need quick opinions on a new compact chart key pattern. Goal: reclaim horizontal pixels for dense dashboards while keeping series mapping discoverable and keyboard/screenreader friendly. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-key-proposal

Tom: TL;DR: compact inline key (swatch + 2-4 char abbrev) + single "Expand key" control that opens an inline drawer with full names + search. On very small panels, drawer becomes stacked legend below the chart.

Leah: Agree. Accessibility constraints:
- The "Expand key" must be a semantic <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Abbrev items need accessible names: visual "API" but SR reads "Payments API" via aria-label.
- When drawer opens, move focus to list root and enable Arrow navigation.

Ibrahim: Implementation notes from eng:
- We can reuse Drawer component; popover isn't reliable in embedded dashboards.
- I'll add a util formatNumberAccessible to return long-unit strings for aria-labels of ticks (e.g., visual "2.5K" -> SR "2,500 milliseconds").
- We'll debounce aria-live messages 200ms and coalesce frequent toggles.

Aria: Microcopy proposals (please critique):
- Expand button closed state label: "Open series key, 6 series".
- Open state label: "Close series key".
- Drawer SR hint when opened: "Series key expanded. Use Arrow keys to navigate, Space to toggle visibility."

Leah: Slight tweak: for the closed state use "Show series key, 6 series" so it reads more like action. Also add a visually-hidden status text near the button that reads "Series key collapsed" so AT users get an immediate state.

Tom: UX detail: show a tiny caret next to the button, increase hit target to 44px, and for panels with >8 series include a small search input at top of drawer. Keep smoothing control out of the key; put it in the overflow menu with a short tooltip: "Smoothing emphasizes trend, may obscure spikes." Default = off for perf charts.

Ibrahim: Outliers: product wants to avoid axis inflation. Proposal: show de-emphasized off-chart markers plus a focusable "+n outlier(s)" badge pinned to the chart corner. Badge is a button: aria-label example "Three points outside visible range. Press Enter to include in scale." Clicking expands axis.

Leah: For unit labels: prefer a subtitle line under the axis with both long + short form: e.g., "Latency (milliseconds, ms)". Use compact tick numbers visually and supply aria-labels for each tick value with full wording. When unit auto-changes (K/M), announce via aria-live: "Axis unit changed to thousands". Debounce to avoid chatter.

Aria: Accessibility QA checklist draft:
- Keyboard: Tab order (expand button -> drawer search -> list items -> outlier badge -> chart controls).
- Screenreader: SR reads expand button label; opening drawer announces list count; toggling a series announces "Series X hidden/visible" (coalesced).
- Visual: minimum line stroke 1.5px for thin lines or use high-contrast token.

Tom: I'll prototype the drawer + search and attach a short screencap.

ux-bot: Reminder: UX crit session on Thursday 16:00 UTC if you want live feedback.

Aria: Thanks all. Next steps: @Ibrahim spike formatNumberAccessible + outlier badge behavior; @Tom push prototype; @Leah finalize microcopy. We'll reconvene after the prototype. :sparkles:
